name: Mitel MiCollab
tile_line: Exploited before the patch, no login. In CISA KEV.
tldr: Five bugs in the conferencing part of Mitel MiCollab (AWV) need no login. Attackers used them before the 16 Nov patch, in one case reaching a domain controller within an hour. Patch now and check for a break-in.
summary: Accenture's APEX Labs saw web-shell activity at one victim before 23:00 UTC on 15 Nov, a day before Mitel's patch: the attacker ran its first command 12 minutes after its first request, had root within 30 minutes, used MiCollab's stored LDAP credentials to log in to a domain controller at 32 minutes and later stole databases, and it filtered its requests out of MiCollab's local logs. Accenture links a second organisation's MiCollab server to the same attacker from 9 Nov but doesn't know how it was broken into, and Mitel says using the five bugs together "can significantly amplify their impact" without saying how. A GitHub repository claiming an exploit for CVE-2026-133323 doesn't match Mitel's description, so we don't count it as a public exploit; NVD scores the two worst bugs 9.8.

affected.label: MiCollab, not patched
affected.text: Mitel lists MiCollab 10.3 (10.3.0.18) and earlier as affected. The fix is a patch for 10.3.0.18, so 10.3.0.18 without it is still affected. Mitel doesn't consider versions past End of Support.

affected.label: An attacker can reach AWV
affected.text: All five bugs are in the Audio, Web and Video Conferencing (AWV) component and need no login: a blind command injection (CVE-2026-133323, 10.0), command execution through XML injection with content planted in advance (CVE-2026-133303, 9.0), and three medium bugs that upload files, skip a login check or read some sensitive information. Mitel's workaround is to restrict external access to AWV. At Accenture's victim the attack passed through an internet-facing reverse proxy, and Accenture says a MiVoice Border Gateway web proxy shouldn't be assumed to protect AWV.

do.label: Apply Mitel's patch
do.text: Upgrade to 10.3.0.18 if needed, then apply Mitel's patch from knowledge base article KB000129195, which is restricted: if you can't open it, Mitel says to contact your Mitel Authorized Partner. Mitel also offers upgrading to a later release but names none. Accenture advises taking forensic images of MiCollab and Border Gateway servers before patching or rebuilding them, because that can overwrite evidence, and fixing older MiCollab flaws (MISA-2026-0006) on servers that have fallen behind.

do.label: Cut outside access to AWV
do.text: Mitel's workaround until you can patch: restrict external access to the AWV component. Accenture adds: include any path a MiVoice Border Gateway web proxy publishes.

do.label: Check for a break-in
do.text: Accenture says a server that is patched now may already be compromised, because attacks began before the patch existed. Compare MiCollab's logs with your proxy, gateway or WAF logs, since the attacker filtered its requests out of local logs. Look for web shells such as `shell.asp` under a `pictures` directory, scripts and `.tgz` archives in `/tmp`, round-the-clock HTTPS to unfamiliar hosts, and traffic to `204.76.203.204` or `204.76.203.216`; Accenture lists more indicators. If you find signs, Accenture says to treat it as an Active Directory compromise: reset MiCollab's LDAP connector account and any Kerberoastable service accounts, and rotate administrator, SIP trunk and file-share credentials the server could reach. Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies must also do CISA's forensic triage for CVE-2026-133323 and CVE-2026-133303.

do.label: Why it's Patch now
do.text: CISA lists all five as exploited and they need no login. Accenture saw them used before any patch existed and, at one victim, to reach the domain controller. It says MiCollab is commonly internet-facing, and a reverse proxy in front of it didn't protect AWV.

versions_skip: The fix is a patch on 10.3.0.18 from a customer-only knowledge base article, and Mitel publishes no public release list.
